fix.summary: Direct Fixer apply is authorized for exactly the three accepted classes below. Do not add compatibility, orchestration, new policy fields, or any TypeBox whitespace-pattern repair.

classes.name: Issue44FixerSubprocessSessionEvidence
classes.owner: Issue #44 Fixer subprocess test invocation seam
classes.disposition: Accepted Standards finding. The helper invokes the real Fixer role with --no-session, directly contradicting CLAUDE.md's mandatory role-invocation evidence rule. Replace that flag with the prescribed .ak/work/issues/44/runs/<invocation>/session arrangement and retain stderr.log plus invocation.json in the same run directory. Preserve the production-seam nonzero/no-receipt assertions; do not widen this repair to unrelated pre-Issue-44 subprocess fixtures.

classes.name: Issue44FreeTextTestAnchors
classes.boundary: The cited Fixer policy-prose assertions in test/fixer-auditor.test.ts and the changed Fixer description/prompt-guideline assertions in test/judge-role.test.ts
classes.disposition: Accepted Standards finding. These assertions mechanically freeze natural-language presentation by regex or exact prose, violating the anchoring constitution. Replace them with typed/tool-surface or observable behavioral assertions: active-model dispatch, exact supplied audit inputs, sole decision tool/schema, revise/pass/failure behavior, unchanged candidate projection, and lawful runtime outcomes. Do not remove authority-required byte-delivery checks for Soul/packet/invocation inputs, and do not introduce a test-only production hook or duplicate policy mechanism.

classes.name: FixerAuditProvenanceAtRecorder
classes.boundary: src/recorder/extract.ts Fixer finalization, its generated dist artifact, and test/fixer-recorder.test.ts
classes.disposition: Accepted Spec finding. Recorder currently sets auditPassed:true for any structurally accepted current Fixer result even when toolResult.usage is absent. For ak_fixer_output only, require the complete valid typed Pi tool-result usage that the current Fixer auditor returns before accepting the lifecycle or emitting auditPassed:true; reject a current-shape success with that evidence removed, while retaining the positive audited lifecycle and legacy-leaf red. Leave other roles' existing compatibility behavior unchanged.

details.note:
Adjudication at current HEAD 0dead5c6837b749ec6f5b713783b45759ab2e49e (post-target changes are docket-only):

1. Session finding accepted. test/audit-failure-subprocess.test.ts visibly passes --no-session together with --ak-role fixer. CLAUDE.md contains no test exception and explicitly says role calls use --session-dir rather than --no-session.

2. Anchoring finding accepted in the narrow cited Issue #44 surface. test/fixer-auditor.test.ts regex-matches auditor policy wording, and test/judge-role.test.ts freezes Fixer description/guideline prose. Those are presentation assertions, unlike checks of typed schema, tool identity, model selection, exact supplied inputs, or observable pass/revise/failure behavior.

3. Recorder finding accepted. carriesPackageAuditObservation merely classifies the tool; finalizeAcceptedPair makes usage optional and synthesizes auditPassed:true regardless. test/fixer-recorder.test.ts supplies usage for its green and rejects only a legacy leaf, so it has no unaudited-current red. Authentic Pi evidence is the tool-result usage row: Pi core copies result.usage into the persisted toolResult; current successful audited Judge/Reviewer rows under .ak/work/issues/44/runs contain complete usage, failed pre-audit rows and the unaudited Coder success do not. worker-role.ts likewise projects the successful Fixer audit's usage onto the tool result. This gives Recorder a typed discriminator without parsing acceptance prose.

4. Spec whitespace finding rejected as a false positive. The authority requires nonblank strings to be trim-checked and legal greens to cross both the real TypeBox schema and production validator; it does not require TypeBox alone to reject whitespace. Current Value.Check accepts a whitespace report, but validateFixerOutput rejects it via trim(), so the real submission pipeline rejects before audit/acceptance. Validator-only trim rejection satisfies the stated contract. No TypeBox pattern/format repair is authorized.

Mechanical spot checks passed for fixer-contract, fixer-auditor, and fixer-recorder tests; their passing state does not dispose the accepted missing reds above.
